source: BEE/SAMEEEKSHA 'Manual on Energy Conservation Measures in Ceramic Cluster Morbi' — Table 3 (Production, Small/Medium/Large scale, boxes or pieces/day) cross-referenced with the electricity-consumption-by-scale table (kWh/day by Small/Medium/Large) for Wall Tiles, Floor Tiles, and Sanitary Wares (Vitrified Tiles excluded — its production-by-band row was ambiguous in the source table extraction). Per-product-type kWh-per-unit-output was computed per band, normalised to that product's own 3-band mean, then averaged across the 3 product types. Note: this real data does NOT show a clean monotonic small-worse/large-better pattern (medium is actually the least efficient band on average) — a tension with the separate, undirected economies-of-scale assumption already baked into data-pipeline/scripts/generate_synthetic.py's scale_effect, disclosed rather than silently reconciled.
